title: Heaters from $5 - E.g. Anko 11 Fin Oil Heater $12 - Was $68 - Free C&C or + Delivery ($0 OnePass/C&C/in Store) @ Kmart
body:
Deal: Heaters from $5 - E.g. Anko 11 Fin Oil Heater $12 - Was $68 - Free C&C or + Delivery ($0 OnePass/C&C/in Store) @ Kmart

[BestTechAdvisor] Just remember that the true cost of resistive heaters is in running them.
E.g. the 2kW fan heater at ~30¢/kW = 60¢/hr
Say 5hrs/day, 30 days a month. 5 x 0.60 x 30 = 90
$90/month to run one small, $5 fan heater for just 5hrs/day.
[AustriaBargain] Yes if you need to run it a lot every year then a split system will always be cheaper in the long run.
[BestTechAdvisor] Yep, and heating oneself directly will always be cheaper than heating a room, so layers + electric blankets should be first on everyone's list.
[AUBRX] Doesn't work for trigeminal neuralgia. Some health conditions you need higher ambient temps.
[Mokr] Free energy much cheaper to run. But would want wifi so it's automated.
[askvictor] Easy to put a smart plug in front of it.
[Fuzor] Still much cheaper than running gas ducted systems
[askvictor] Use an oil heater on a free-midday plan, and it can keep the room warmer for more than the 3 hours.
[ssfps] I was going to install a split system in my spare bedroom to replace a resistive heater, but calculated based on occupancy it would take 30 years to break even on the split at current electricity costs. Often these cheap heaters make more sense when it's not a commonly used area.
[jaboday423] Ordered "Oscillating Fan Heater" for $12 on Aug 13, 2026 and now it's $6
[hopper] Note. They no longer accept returns when you buy clearance items with onepass
